The new stressed-syllable framing scopes these examples; it does not assert that brightening never affected unstressed vowels.

source_basis: Fulk §62 pp41–42/PDF53–54; §91 p61/PDF73; Appendix A IV.28 p111/PDF123; V.45 p113/PDF125
section_coverage.assessment: Material stress-scope omission repaired. Correct immediate æ/e/i inputs, rj exception, rr inclusion, vowel-specific l-cluster limits, short ea in healp/eald, later io/eo merger and limited acknowledgement of long-vowel breaking. *hælp is source-printed reconstruction.

source_basis: Fulk §§73–76 pp48–49/PDF60–61; §79 p52/PDF64; §82 p53/PDF65; §109 p78/PDF90; Appendix A IV.18 p110/PDF122; Cook §§15–17, Appendix V
section_coverage.assessment: Front mutation is historically conditioned, with selected nasal-vowel qualification and no generic plural rule. fēt retains its dative-singular identity. dōm/dēman uses Fulk’s explicit *dōm(i)jan; revised wording identifies the lost conditioning sound. eald/ieldra/ieldest and hātan/hǣtt preserve established forms. helpan/hilpð and ēo/īe are explicitly separated from a falsely single-stage late mutation.

source_basis: Fulk §71 pp45–46/PDF57–58; §119 p85/PDF97; §111d p79/PDF91; Appendix A IV.31,35 p112/PDF124; Appendix B I.3 p118/PDF130, I.5 and III.12 p119/PDF131
section_coverage.assessment: geat/gatu and giefan/geaf/gēafon/giefen retain the stated West Saxon and quantity contrasts. Breaking and palatal diphthongization remain distinct and ordered. Back mutation includes the single-consonant/labial/liquid restrictions and following-a limitation. heofon/hefon is correctly identified as a newly arranged comparison; the literal source parenthesis is hefon beside hefen. hēah/hēh has explicit Late West Saxon scope, distinct from wider Anglian smoothing, and all source-only variants have learner lookup routes.

source_basis: Fulk §135a–d pp103–104/PDF115–116; §67 p44/PDF56; Appendix A III.4–6 p109/PDF121
section_coverage.assessment: cēlan and source-printed *kōljan explain chronological opacity without a universal spelling rule. Palatalization uncertainty is retained. Gemination has the light-syllable condition and r exception. Gothic bidjan is explicitly a cognate, not an ancestor or OE entry. Added §7 pointer resolves the optional definition-access issue.

The bounded ordinary-noun account distinguishes vowel length from stem weight: hof/hofu, word/word, wīf/wīf are sound examples. hēafdes and analogical hēafodes are correctly distinguished. Syncope is not presented as indiscriminate deletion. *seohan/sēon and short seoh preserve exact quantities; contraction and compensatory lengthening are distinguished. Supplied dwelling/wife senses are declared course-sense alignments under SH-A01.

source_basis: Fulk §§84–85 p57/PDF69; §91 p61/PDF73; §87 p58/PDF70; Appendix A II pp108–109/PDF120–121 and VI pp113–114/PDF125–126; Cook §37 p25/PDF41
section_coverage.assessment: All four drīfan/helpan principal parts are coexisting labelled columns. healp is correctly explained by inherited grade plus later breaking, with hilpð separated. Cook’s actual cweðan/cweden pair supports the consonant example; Fulk supports Verner’s inherited voicing and later changes. The account explicitly distinguishes this from ordinary OE fricative voicing and arbitrary ð/d spelling.

findings.location: §3 opening definition and breaking table; reflected in §9 summary
findings.finding: The initial definition and input table omitted the restriction to stressed vowels, so an inexperienced reader could overextend the breaking rule.
findings.source: Fulk Appendix A V.45, printed p113/PDF125 explicitly excludes breaking in unstressed syllables.
findings.requested_change: State stressed-vowel scope locally in the rule and input heading.
findings.resolution: SH-AUTH-REV01 adds the qualifier to the definition and heading, carries it into the summary and adds the exact source note. Related stress framing was added in §§2/5 without falsely excluding unstressed brightening or mutation.

findings.finding: Light syllable first occurs before its definition in §7.
The phrase removed the old ending is broader than necessary because -an survives; the intended point is loss of the conditioning sound.
findings.requested_change: Identify the conditioning sound as the element lost.
findings.resolution: SH-AUTH-REV03 now says removed the conditioning sound. The following sentence explicitly retains -an.

acceptance.learner_intelligibility: The optional appendix defines its historical terms, gives supplied meanings and identities, separates reconstructions and Gothic, retains source-only-form lookup routes and avoids new IPA. The selected examples explain real course alternations without claiming automatic derivation of every paradigm.
